name: Sukkot (Feast of Tabernacles)
description: A seven-day festival of joy commemorating the wilderness wanderings.
biblicalBasis: Leviticus 23:33-43: "You shall dwell in booths for seven days... so that future generations may know that I made the Israelites live in booths when I brought them out of Egypt." Deuteronomy 16:13-15: "You shall rejoice with your son and your daughter, your male servant and your female servant." Nehemiah 8:14-18 regarding the resumption of Sukkot after the exile. John 7:37-38: On the last day of the great feast, Jesus cried out, "If anyone thirsts, let him come to me and drink."
significance: Sukkot reminds us that life is provisional—booths are fragile, open to the sky. Humanity lives by God's daily provision, not by our own walls. The water-drawing ceremony in the temple pointed to God's blessing and rain—Jesus connects to this when he offers living water (John 7). The Feast of Tabernacles is the most joyful of the festivals—the "season of our joy" (zman simchatenu).
liturgicalContext: Celebrated from Tishri 15–21. The lulav (palm branch, myrtle, willow) and etrog (citrus fruit) are waved in all directions. Family and friends gather in sukkah booths for meals. Hoshanot processions around the synagogue's bimah. Concludes with Shemini Atzeret and Simchat Torah (Rejoicing of the Torah).
history: One of the three pilgrimage festivals (shalosh regalim) when all Israel went up to Jerusalem. Solomon's temple dedication took place during Sukkot (1 Kings 8). During the Second Temple period, the water-drawing ceremony and the illumination in the temple court were spectacular events. Zechariah 14:16-19 prophesies that all nations will celebrate Sukkot in the Messianic age.
otConnections: The pillar of cloud and pillar of fire in the wilderness (Exodus 13:21-22)—God's protective presence symbolized by the booths. 1 Kings 8—Solomon's temple dedication during Sukkot. Zechariah 14:16-19 regarding the future celebration of Sukkot by all nations. Nehemiah 8:14-18 concerning the great rediscovery of the Sukkot celebration.
